note: پارٹی means a political party/group but also a social party/gathering. The social meaning is too common to omit.
دل centrally means heart and also mind/feelings/desire in many expressions. 'Wish; attention' alone does not give the learner the core semantic range.
باہر is primarily the locative adverb/noun outside/outdoors. 'Eminent, excelling' is unrelated/noisy for a modern learner entry.
حضرت is an honorific title used for revered/respected persons, saints, prophets, or elders. 'Gentleman' is much too narrow and can misrepresent register.
proposed_english: honorific for a revered/respected person; His/Her Holiness; respected sir/lady (context-dependent)

note: بھارتی means Indian, either adjective or person/nationality noun. 'Name' POS is not appropriate.
تاہم functions as an adversative conjunction/discourse connector ('however/nevertheless'), not merely a lexical adverb.
تاکہ is a subordinating conjunction meaning so that/in order that. 'Closed-class' is too vague.
جگہ should lead with place/location/space/site. 'Post; station' are context-specific and should not obscure the central meaning.
بند centrally means closed/shut and also a dam/barrier or band/stanza in specific contexts. 'Bun' is dictionary contamination and should be removed.
فوجی means soldier as a noun and military/army-related as an adjective. Noun-only POS omits the adjectival use.
تھیں is the feminine plural past form of ہونا ('were'), not an unspecified closed-class item.
Central expression sense omitted and gloss is overlong/noisy.
کمی means lack/shortage/deficiency/decrease. The caste-related dictionary sense is derogatory/obsolete and should not be presented without register context in a general learner entry.
Productive owner/possessor sense omitted.
proposed_english: sir; mister; gentleman; owner; possessor; person having/endowed with (especially in compounds)

note: یعنی is a discourse/conjunctive expression meaning that is/namely/i.e./meaning. Interjection POS is misleading.
proposed_english: that is; namely; i.e.; meaning/in other words

note: ہونا means to be/exist/become/happen. 'To want' is incorrect for this verb.
proposed_english: to be; to exist; to become; to happen

note: یہی is an emphatic demonstrative meaning this very/this same/exactly this. 'Closed-class' is too vague.
proposed_english: this very; this same; exactly this

note: بغیر is a postposition/preposition meaning without/except for. Adjective POS and 'lacking' as the headword meaning are not the clearest learner analysis.
وی is the name/representation of the Latin letter V, especially in acronyms. 'Content word' is not a POS.
بڑا centrally means big/large/great/elder and can intensify as very. The source omits the basic 'big/large' meaning.
proposed_english: big; large; great; elder/older; very (intensifying use)

note: ناظم is a noun meaning administrator/manager/organizer/coordinator; it can also mean poet/composer in older/literary usage. Adjective POS is incorrect.

فراہم in modern Urdu is learned as provided/supplied/available, especially in فراہم کرنا 'to provide'. 'Gathered, collected, obtained' reflects etymological/older senses and is poor as the core learner gloss.
زلزلے is an inflected form of زلزلہ and must explicitly give the lexical meaning earthquake/earthquakes rather than only inflection labels.
قبل means before/prior to/ago, often in سے قبل. It functions adverbially and in postpositional expressions; the current gloss is acceptable but POS can be clearer.
